⏸ OEM HOLD — Main journal taper (R11)CRANK prints the main taper limit as 0.001 in and 0.01 mm. These are not the same: 0.001 in = 0.0254 mm, and 0.01 mm = 0.000394 in. The sheet shows your reading against both and will not give an OEM PASS until Cummins confirms which is correct.
Journal size (R12)Set Rod Journal Size and Main Journal Size in the job card. Standard limits apply only to STD. Undersize rods: .010 / .020 / .030 / .040 in. Undersize mains: .010 / .020 in. Undersize minimums are not in the audit register, so an undersize crank shows HOLD until the regrind limits (Bulletin 3666008) are entered. Record each journal's actual size.
Source: CRANK 001-016 · QuickServe manual 3666206 (audit 19-Oct-2026)
Crankshaft Measurement Procedure
WarningCrankshaft weighs more than 23 kg [50 lb]. Use nylon lift sling 3375957 around journals #3 and #4.
  1. Polish journals with fine crocus cloth. Brush every oil drilling.
  2. Steam-clean and dry with compressed air. Blow out threaded holes and drillings.
  3. Inspect threaded holes; repair with insert kit 3822709. More than two damaged holes on one end = replace crankshaft.
  4. Measure front and rear seal contact areas for a wear groove. MAX 0.25 mm [0.010 in].
  5. Inspect all journals for deep scoring or heat discolouration.
  6. Identify journal size (STD or the stamped undersize) and set it in the job card.
  7. Measure each rod journal with a 2–3 in micrometer, and each main journal with a 3–4 in micrometer.
  8. Out-of-round: enter the two readings 90° apart (A and B). Taper: enter the front-end and rear-end readings. The sheet works out the difference.
  9. Measure thrust face width at journal #4, rear seal flange OD and damper pilot OD.
  10. Oil the crank and cover it if it is not going in right away.
Source: CRANK 001-016 · QuickServe manual 3666206 (audit 19-Oct-2026)

⏸ OEM HOLD — Clearance checking method (R07)The old step-1-only method (37 ft-lb, shells in, crank installed) is withdrawn. A bore gauge cannot read the bearing bore with the crank in it, and CRANK does not give a light-clamp method. Proposed method (engineering inference, not an OEM quote): crank out, caps tightened to the full 50 → 95 N·m → 60° assembly torque, read bore with bearing installed. Cummins must confirm the checking torque and whether bolts may be re-used after a check. Until then clearance results show HOLD, never OEM PASS.
Bearing identificationUpper bearings have two oil holes; lower bearings have none. #4 journal uses the flanged thrust bearing. Caps are numbered from the front, numbers toward the CAMSHAFT side.
Source: MAIN 001-006 · CRANK 001-016 · QuickServe manual 3666206 (audit 19-Oct-2026)

Lubrication (R10)Bearing backs and block saddles: clean and DRY. Bearing working faces: clean engine oil. Main bolt threads and under the bolt heads: clean engine oil — let excess oil drain off before installing.
Critical checkThe crankshaft must turn freely after all caps are tightened. If not, loosen all caps and check bearing size and fit.
End playDial indicator on the crank nose. Push crank rearward, zero, push forward, read. Below 0.005 in: loosen caps, push crank fore and aft, re-torque in sequence.
Source: MAIN 001-006 · QuickServe manual 3666206 (audit 19-Oct-2026)
Main Bearing Installation Procedure
  1. Mark caps before removal. Do not pry caps off — walk them off with two cap bolts.
  2. Clean caps, saddles and shells with solvent; Scotch-Brite 7448 on seating surfaces. No wire brush on bearings.
  3. Inspect shells for pitting, flaking, corrosion, tang damage or deep scratches.
  4. Fit new shells matching journal size. Upper (two holes) in block, lower (no holes) in caps; #4 flanged thrust bearing.
  5. Keep bearing backs and saddles dry. Oil the bearing working faces.
  6. Lower the crank in. Fit caps in numbered position, numbers toward the camshaft.
  7. Oil bolt threads and under heads; let excess drain.
  8. Tighten bolts 1 → 14 (sequence tab): 50 N·m, then 95 N·m, then 60°.
  9. Check the crank turns freely. Measure and record end play.
  10. Bearing clearance: record only by the HOLD method once Cummins approves it. Do not use step-1-only readings.
Source: MAIN 001-006 · CRANK 001-016 · QuickServe manual 3666206 (audit 19-Oct-2026)

Source: CRANK 001-016 · CONROD 001-014 · ROD 001-005 · QuickServe manual 3666206 (audit 19-Oct-2026)
Con Rod Bearing Installation Procedure
  1. Before removal, mark each shell U/L and journal number. Check rod and cap serial numbers match.
  2. Clean caps, fasteners and bearings; Scotch-Brite 7448 on seating surfaces. No wire brush on bearings.
  3. Inspect shells. Fit new shells matching journal size. Backs dry, working faces oiled.
  4. Fit the cap: number matches rod, tang toward the camshaft.
  5. Oil threads and under nuts. Tighten alternately: 30 N·m, then 70 N·m.
  6. HOLD: apply the final angle only once Cummins confirms 60° or 90° for the fitted hardware. Record the angle used.
  7. Check the crank turns freely after each cap. Measure side clearance with a feeler gauge.
Source: ROD 001-005 · PISTON 001-054 · QuickServe manual 3666206 (audit 19-Oct-2026)

Liner inspectionVertical scratches that catch a fingernail, or heavy polish with no hone marks = replace. Do not hone or deglaze liners.

Liner Protrusion — Seat, Unclamp, Then Measure (R13)
  1. Seat the liner with two clamps at 68 N·m [50 ft-lb].
  2. Remove the clamps. The reading is taken unclamped.
  3. Use gauge 3823495. Read protrusion at 4 points, 90° apart. Enter all four readings.
  4. If the readings vary by more than 0.001 in across 180°, reclamp, recheck, and inspect if it persists.
  5. Adjacent cylinders may differ by no more than 0.002 in (the sheet works this out).

⏸ OEM HOLD — Installed protrusion acceptance (R14)LINER's install section gives 0.001–0.005 in with no used-block exception, but its initial-check table allows 0.000 in for a used block. The sheet checks your readings against both and holds the result until Cummins resolves which applies to the installed liner.
Source: LINER 001-028 · QuickServe manual 3666206 (audit 19-Oct-2026)
Piston & Ring Installation Procedure
  1. Measure each liner bore in 4 directions at top and bottom. Record the largest.
  2. Record initial out-of-round and taper (reuse limits 0.002 in). After installing, recheck out-of-round (0.003 in max).
  3. Measure liner-to-block casting clearance (0.009 in min).
  4. Confirm the piston kit from the ESN parts listing (R17).
  5. Square each NEW ring 89 mm [3.5 in] below the deck in the liner it will run in. Measure and record every gap.
  6. Fit rings, stagger gaps 120°. Fit pin retainers. FRONT mark on the piston toward the front of the engine.
  7. Oil the bore and rings. Ring compressor on, rod tang toward the camshaft side.
  8. Fit the rod cap (Section 3 torque HOLD applies). Measure side clearance; crank must turn freely.
Source: LINER 001-028 · RINGS 001-047 · PISTON 001-054 · QuickServe manual 3666206 (audit 19-Oct-2026)

TSI SHOP RULE — Flatness 0.006 inTSI may still choose a tighter 0.006 in full-length rule. It is shown here as a shop rule only — the OEM limits are the cards above.
⏸ OEM HOLD — Valve spring load test height (R20)HEAD gives 359–397 N [80.7–89.2 lb] with tool 3375182, but the test compression height was not in the audited text. Get the full test setup before using the load as a pass/fail test. The old "2.16 in minimum free length" was wrong and has been removed.
Source: HEAD 002-004 · QuickServe manual 3666206 (audit 19-Oct-2026)
Cylinder Head Inspection Procedure
  1. Get the machine shop's paperwork: guides, seat work, pressure test method and result.
  2. Clean carbon with abrasive pad 3823258 and solvent. Inspect the deck for cracks, erosion and hot spots.
  3. Flatness: end to end (0.008 in max), side to side (0.003 in max), then local checks with a 2 in straightedge — a 0.001 in feeler must not fit. If it fits, resurface or replace.
  4. Pressure test (shop): fixture capscrews 80 N·m [59 ft-lb] — this is the TEST FIXTURE only, never a head-bolt step. Regulate 276 kPa [40 psi], immerse the head completely in water at 60°C [140°F]. Any leak = reject. No 3-minute hold is specified.
  5. Measure valve recess below the deck on all 12 valves.
  6. Recess out of limits: first try a new valve. If that brings it back in limits, grind the old seat and use the new valve. Only then replace the insert.
  7. Check guide ID and guide height (top of guide to bottom of recess) against the shop record.
  8. Valve stem height above the head may be recorded for reference only.
Source: HEAD 002-004 · QuickServe manual 3666206 (audit 19-Oct-2026)

Notes & Cautions
Which branch? (R02)A new block OR any new capscrew = Branch B. Only when the block AND all 26 capscrews are reused do you use Branch A. Record both answers before torquing.
Capscrew acceptanceReused capscrews: check threads, corrosion, reduced diameter and free length with gauge 3823921. OEM maximum free length: short 81.5 mm [3.2 in], long 162.6 mm [6.4 in]. Use the gauge — the inch figures are rounded.
PreparationNew gasket aligned, dowels seated. Oil threads and under the bolt heads with engine oil. Run all bolts in finger-tight first.
Angle methodEach capscrew top has a dot and a window. Mark the head beside the dot and turn until the mark is in the window, or use angle gauge 3823878 (1/2 in) / 3823879 (3/4 in).
Not "centre out"Follow the numbered OEM order exactly. "Centre out" on its own is not the instruction.
Source: HEAD 002-004 · QuickServe manual 3666206 (audit 19-Oct-2026)

Model checkThese are C8.3G / C Gas Plus clearances. L Gas Plus (0.014 / 0.030 in) is a different model — do not use. Keep the G8.3 model and rating on the job card.
TSI SHOP RULE — Cam lobe pittingThe checklist's "no pitting" rule is stricter than CAM, which gives detailed allowable pitting criteria.
Source: LASH 003-004 · ROCKER 003-008 · CAM 001-008 · QuickServe manual 3666206 (audit 19-Oct-2026)
Valve Lash — Two Crank Positions
  1. Engine cold (below 60°C [140°F]). Remove the valve cover.
  2. Rotate until #1 is at TDC compression (#6 exhaust closing, #6 intake opening).
  3. STEP A — set Intake 1, 2, 4 and Exhaust 1, 3, 5.
  4. Slight drag on the feeler is correct. Hold the screw, tighten the locknut to 24 N·m [212 in-lb], then recheck that valve.
  5. Mark the damper. Rotate the crankshaft 360°.
  6. STEP B — set Intake 3, 5, 6 and Exhaust 2, 4, 6. Locknut and recheck each.
  7. Final recheck: go back to the Step A position and recheck the Step A valves, then turn 360° and recheck the Step B valves. One crank position does not check all 12.
  8. Fit new capscrew O-rings and the cover seal. Valve cover 24 N·m [212 in-lb].
Rocker assembly (R25)Seat each adjusting-screw ball in its pushrod socket. Oil pedestal capscrew threads and under heads; torque 55 N·m [41 ft-lb].
Source: LASH 003-004 · ROCKER 003-008 · QuickServe manual 3666206 (audit 19-Oct-2026)

Reference corrected (R26)The applicable pump procedure is 007-031 (not 007-019). It is a gerotor pump with a back plate — not a gear pump with an integral relief valve.
TSI SHOP RULE — Oil pressure 40 psiA 40 psi rated-speed minimum may be kept as a TSI rule, but OIL gives 10 psi at low idle and 30 psi at 1400 rpm or torque peak. Confirm the generator rated-speed value on the engine data sheet.
Source: PUMP 007-031 · SUCTION 007-035 · PAN 007-025 · OIL 018-017 · QuickServe manual 3666206 (audit 19-Oct-2026)
Oil Pump — Removal, Inspection & Installation (007-031)
  1. Prep: remove the drive belt, the vibration damper / crank pulley and the front gear cover.
  2. Remove the pump. Inspect the gerotor rotors, back plate and housing for scoring, pitting or chipping. Check the drive gear and idler pin.
  3. Clean with solvent and a soft brush; dry. No wire brush on rotors or bores.
  4. Fill and lubricate the pump with clean oil so it primes quickly.
  5. Install with the TOP mark up and the idler pin in its locating bore. The back plate seats in the block bore — the flange does NOT touch the block. Do not pull the flange flush.
  6. Tighten the 4 mounting capscrews to 24 N·m [18 ft-lb] in the OEM illustrated order.
  7. Measure backlash checks A and B with the adjoining gear held still. Both 0.076–0.330 mm [0.003–0.013 in].
  8. Suction tube: new gasket (do not assume an O-ring). Finger-tight and aligned first, then tube-to-block, bracket-to-block, tube-to-bracket. 6 mm: 10 N·m [89 in-lb]; 10 mm: 24 N·m [18 ft-lb].
  9. Oil pan: same gasket/RTV arrangement as fitted, sealant at the specified rail joints, 28 N·m [248 in-lb] in the OEM sequence.
  10. After start: oil pressure at least 10 psi at low idle and 30 psi at 1400 rpm (hot).
Source: PUMP 007-031 · SUCTION 007-035 · PAN 007-025 · OIL 018-017 · QuickServe manual 3666206 (audit 19-Oct-2026)

⚠ CAUTION Monitor oil pressure, coolant temperature, and oil temperature continuously during the break-in run. Shut down immediately if any parameter exceeds limits. Do not leave the unit unattended during the first hour.
⏸ NOT THE OEM RUN-IN (R31)Cummins RUN 014-006 uses 3–5 min idle, staged speeds and loads with temperature and stable-blowby gates, full-load checks and a 3–5 min cool-down. This 4-hour load bank run is a TSI / customer acceptance protocol. Get the G8.3 generator run-in instruction before calling it the OEM run-in. ROAD 014-004 is a vehicle program and does not apply.
⏸ LIMITS NOT OEM-VERIFIED (R32, R33)Oil temperature, voltage, frequency, battery and timing tolerances on this page are TSI/customer rules. Gas pressures are not supported by the manual's 018-016 page (it shows diesel data). Confirm regulator/mixer identity, pressure tap and static vs flowing condition for CPL 2474.
Load Bank Break-In Procedure
  1. Verify engine oil level, coolant level, and fuel supply before starting.
  2. Start engine and warm up (TSI protocol: 10–15 minutes no-load; the OEM RUN procedure uses 3–5 minutes idle). Verify oil pressure is present within 10 seconds of start.
  3. Connect load bank to generator output terminals. Verify correct voltage and phase rotation before applying load.
  4. Use the Break-In Calculator below to determine target amperage. Set load bank to 75% of engine rated HP.
  5. Apply load gradually — bring to 25%, then 50%, then 75% over 5–10 minutes.
  6. Take a baseline reading when the target load is first reached. Then record all parameters every 30 minutes for 4 hours (8 readings, T+0:30 to T+4:00).
  7. Monitor for oil leaks, coolant leaks, unusual noises, or abnormal vibration throughout the run.
  8. At completion, reduce load gradually to zero, then allow engine to cool at no-load for 5 minutes before shutdown.
  9. After shutdown, check oil level, coolant level, and inspect for any leaks or loose connections.
  10. Record final ignition timing and verify it has not drifted during the run.
Acceptance Criteria — TSI / customer protocol (not OEM-verified)
  1. Oil Pressure: Minimum 30 PSI throughout the run, no downward trend (OEM minimum: 30 psi at 1400 rpm / torque peak).
  2. Coolant Temperature: Stable below 210°F (TSI stop point; OEM maximum 212°F). Must reach and hold operating temperature within 30 minutes.
  3. Oil Temperature: Stable below 250°F. Should stabilize within first hour.
  4. Voltage: All three phases within ±2% of rated voltage throughout run.
  5. Frequency: 60 Hz ±0.5 Hz throughout run.
  6. Load: Held at the calculator target throughout the run — 75% of engine rated HP expressed as mechanical kW (HP × 0.75 × 0.746). Generator electrical kW will read lower than this because of alternator losses; that is expected and is not a failure. Record generator kW as a percentage of nameplate for information only.
  7. Battery Voltage: 13.2–14.8V (charging) throughout run.
  8. Fuel Pressure: Stable — no significant drop during run indicating fuel supply issue.
  9. No leaks of oil, coolant, or fuel at any point during or after the run.
  10. Ignition Timing: Within ±2° of specification at end of run.

Amps assume a balanced 3-phase resistive load at PF 1.0 and treat the target as electrical kW, so the engine runs slightly above 75% once alternator losses are added.
